SETUP with AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN option (DELETE alias=0). No endpoint accepts it. A server: Section 9.1.4: "If a server receives Alias Type DELETE (0x0) or USE_ALIAS (0x2) in a SETUP message, it MUST close the session with ROLE_VIOLATION." A client: SETUP is the server's first message, so alias 0 is not registered, and Section 8.9: "The receiver of a message referencing an Alias that is not currently registered MUST reject the message with UNKNOWN_AUTH_TOKEN_ALIAS."
vectors.error_detail: Alias Type DELETE in SETUP: ROLE_VIOLATION at a server, UNKNOWN_AUTH_TOKEN_ALIAS at a client

vectors.description: SETUP with PATH, AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN (REGISTER), and AUTHORITY options
non-canonical SETUP — PATH option string length (4) is encoded as a 2-byte varint (8004) instead of the canonical 1-byte form (04); decoders MUST accept

SETUP with MAX_FILTER_RANGES option (Type 0x06) set to 4 — permits up to 4 total Ranges across a subscription's Range Filter parameters. The default of 0 forbids Range Filters entirely (Section 9.1.6)
SETUP with MAX_REQUEST_UPDATES option (Type 0x08) set to 16 — max unacknowledged REQUEST_UPDATEs per request stream. PUBLISH_STATE_NOTIFY (0x22) is not counted against this limit (Section 9.10)
SETUP with both MAX_FILTER_RANGES (0x06 = 8) and MAX_REQUEST_UPDATES (0x08 = 32) options; demonstrates delta-type ordering

SETUP with MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_SIZE (Option Type 0x09) set to 65535, its minimum and its default. The draft does not settle the option's encoding. Section 9.1.8 says "The value is encoded as a variable-length integer", but 0x09 is odd, and an odd Type is followed by a Length and that many bytes (Section 8.3). This corpus uses the Length-prefixed form, 09 03 c0ffff, because a receiver that does not know 0x09 can only skip it by its parity (Section 9.1: "Receivers MUST ignore unrecognized Setup Options"). The bare form would be 09 c0ffff

SETUP with PATH "/moq", MAX_REQUEST_UPDATES=4 and MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_SIZE=1048576. The last option's Delta Type is 1, from 0x08, and its value is the three-byte vi64 d00000 behind a Length of 3, the Length-prefixed form max-control-message-size explains
SETUP with a 100-byte body: one MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION option with a 98-byte value. The Message Length is the one-byte vi64 64 (Section 9). A 16-bit Length would be 00 64 and a QUIC varint 40 64
SETUP with a 300-byte body: one MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION option with a 297-byte value. The Message Length is the two-byte vi64 812c; a 16-bit Length would be 01 2c

SETUP with a 16384-byte body: one MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION option with a 16381-byte value. The Message Length is the minimal three-byte vi64 c04000, since two bytes hold at most 16383. It is within the default MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_SIZE of 65535 (Section 9.1.8)

SETUP with a 65536-byte body: one MOQT_IMPLEMENTATION option with a 65532-byte value, so the Message Length is the three-byte vi64 c10000. Section 9: "If an endpoint receives a control message with a length larger than its MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_SIZE, it MUST close the session with FIELD_LENGTH_EXCEEDED." Section 9.1.8: "Until an endpoint receives the peer's SETUP, it uses the default value, including for SETUP itself." The default is 65535. The option value is within the 2^16-1 byte limit of Section 8.3, so the Length is the only fault
vectors.error_detail: Length 65536 is larger than the default MAX_CONTROL_MESSAGE_SIZE of 65535: FIELD_LENGTH_EXCEEDED

vectors.description: non-canonical SETUP — the PATH option of path-option behind a Message Length of 6 written as the three-byte vi64 c00006. Section 8.1: "Variable-length integers do not need to be encoded using the minimum number of bytes; any encoding length that can represent the value is valid." The same slot holds any Length up to 2097151. Decode-only
